basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE BANGSAMORO ATTORNEY-GENERAL'S OFFICE, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND POWERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after complete publication in at least one newspaper of general circulation in the Bangsamoro region
basic_information.title_note: The page footers of the signed copy read “Page X of BAA 7”, although the act is numbered 5 in its own heading and on the official index. Recorded as enacted.

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates the office of the region's chief government lawyer — the Bangsamoro Attorney-General — who advises the Chief Minister and ministries, represents the government in court, and must be told about every case the government is involved in.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 8, Article XVI of the Organic Law provides for a Bangsamoro Attorney-General. This act sets up the office, its powers and its funding.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The Bangsamoro Government has a single chief legal counsel with power to demand information from any official, summon any employee except Members of Parliament, and represent the region in court and in international negotiations.
who_will_be_affected: Anyone in litigation with the Bangsamoro Government
Every Bangsamoro ministry, agency and office
Government legal officers, who form a Legal Liaison Network under the Attorney-General
Lawyers in private practice engaged by ministries, whose engagement must be reported
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2020 — 15 days after complete publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The region has a chief government lawyer who represents it in court, advises the Chief Minister, and must be notified of every case involving the Bangsamoro Government within 3 days.
in_practice: The Attorney-General is the chief legal counsel of the Bangsamoro Government, with the rank of a cabinet member
Appointed by the Chief Minister, and coterminous with the appointing authority because the position is primarily confidential
Must be a Philippine Bar member in good standing, a bonafide resident of the BARMM, with at least 10 years in practice (6 for the Assistant)
Four divisions: Litigation; Legal Research and Opinion; Intergovernmental Relations; and Administrative and Finance
May require any officer or employee to furnish information, and summon any of them — except Members of Parliament and their immediate staff — to explain or assist
All ministries must notify the Attorney-General of all litigation within 3 days, and no case may be filed for the government without prior notice
The Legal Research and Opinion Division formulates and reviews policy on Shari'ah matters and gives written Shari'ah opinions to the Chief Minister and Cabinet
₱15,000,000 for personal services and ₱3,000,000 for initial operations

for_specific_groups.Anyone suing or being sued by the Bangsa: The Litigation Division represents the government in all civil and administrative proceedings, and in criminal cases where it is the plaintiff.
for_specific_groups.Ministries and agencies: You must notify the Attorney-General of all litigation within 3 days, and report any engagement of a private lawyer for records purposes.
for_specific_groups.Government legal officers: You form part of the Legal Liaison Network, chaired ex officio by the Attorney-General.
for_specific_groups.Members of Parliament: You and your immediate staff are expressly outside the Attorney-General's summons power.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Government, its ministries, agencies, offices and instrumentalities.
what_you_can_do: If you are litigating against a Bangsamoro ministry, expect the Attorney-General's Office to appear
Note that ministries may seek the Attorney-General's opinion on constitutional issues
watch_out_for: Section 17 bars criminal, civil or administrative suits against the Attorney-General, the Assistant and subordinate officers in respect of proceedings or the discharge of functions under the act — an unusually broad immunity.
The appointment is coterminous with the Chief Minister, so the government's chief legal counsel changes with the government.
Legal service to a ministry is provided only where no conflict of interest arises and the agency lacks legal capacity itself.
Seeking the Attorney-General's opinion on constitutional issues is permissive — ministries may do so, not must.

key_terms_explained.Chief legal counsel: The government's own lawyer — advising it, drafting for it and representing it, rather than prosecuting crime.
key_terms_explained.Coterminous: The appointment ends when the appointing authority's term ends.
key_terms_explained.Motu proprio: On the official's own initiative, without being asked.
key_terms_explained.Case build-up: Assembling the evidence and legal basis of a case before it is filed.
key_terms_explained.Legal Liaison Network: All legal officers across the Bangsamoro Government, coordinating under the Attorney-General as ex officio chair.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 27 December 2019, approved by the Chief Minister on 14 January 2020.

benefits.headline: One chief government lawyer, with sight of every case the region is involved in.

direct_benefits.benefit: Consistent legal representation for the Bangsamoro Government in court
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The region and, indirectly, litigants facing a single competent counterparty

direct_benefits.benefit: Written Shari'ah opinions to the Chief Minister and Cabinet, and Shari'ah policy review
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The Bangsamoro Government and, through it, the public

direct_benefits.benefit: Representation of the Bangsamoro in international litigation, negotiations and conferences

indirect_benefits: A coordinated Legal Liaison Network across all ministries
Direct transfer of the office's budget, rather than routing through a parent ministry
Advice available to any committee of Parliament on request
limitations: Broad immunity from suit for the office's principals.
Appointment tied to the Chief Minister's term.
No power to summon Members of Parliament or their staff.

for_ministries: Notify the Attorney-General of all litigation within 3 days
Give prior notice before filing any case for the Bangsamoro Government
Report engagement of any private lawyer for records purposes
Furnish information and attend when summoned

what_is_prohibited: No case or litigation of any kind may be filed or commenced on behalf of the Bangsamoro Government, its ministries, commissions, agencies or offices without prior notice to the Attorney-General.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: No sanction is stated for a ministry that fails to give the required notice of litigation.

where_to_complain.oversight: Office of the Chief Minister, before which administrative complaints are lodged and on which the Attorney-General recommends action
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no public complaints procedure, and Section 17 restricts suits against the office's principals.

everyday_scenarios: A contractor sues a Bangsamoro ministry. The ministry must notify the Attorney-General within 3 days, and the Litigation Division represents the government.
A ministry wants to hire an outside law firm. It may, but must notify the Attorney-General of the engagement for records purposes.
The Cabinet needs to know whether a proposed policy complies with Shari'ah. The Legal Research and Opinion Division formulates and reviews Shari'ah policy and issues written opinions.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Attorney-General's Office Act of 2019”.

Sections 3–4 — Creates the Bangsamoro Attorney-General's Office pursuant to Section 8, Article XVI of Republic Act 11054, with the Attorney-General as chief legal counsel of the Bangsamoro Government.

Sections 5–7 — The Chief Minister appoints the Attorney-General and Assistant Attorney-General; in line with the primarily confidential nature of the positions, both appointments are coterminous with the appointing authority. The Attorney-General appoints all officials and employees below the Assistant, subject to civil service law. Qualifications: Philippine citizenship, membership of the Philippine Bar in good standing, recognised competence, bonafide residence in the BARMM, and 10 years in practice for the Attorney-General or six for the Assistant. The Attorney-General holds the rank of a cabinet member at Salary Grade 28, the Assistant at 27.

Section 8 — Functions: render legal opinions on all legal matters brought by Parliament, the Chief Minister and ministries, and give advice to officials on his or her own initiative or on request; review, vet and interpret local, national and international documents, contracts and agreements for the Chief Minister; recommend action on administrative complaints lodged before the Office of the Chief Minister; assist the Inter-Governmental Relations body when called upon; and provide legal services facilitating, promoting and monitoring democracy, the rule of law and good governance.

Section 9 — Powers: require any officer or employee of the Bangsamoro Government to furnish information relating to their duties; summon any officer or employee — except Members of Parliament and their immediate staff — to explain or assist, including case build-up on any matter that is or could be the subject of litigation by or against the government; administer oaths; propose to Parliament the establishment, merger or abolition of divisions subject to Cabinet approval; and, on request, appear and advise on any legal matter in any committee of the Bangsamoro Parliament.

Section 11 — Four divisions. The Litigation Division represents the government in all civil and administrative proceedings and in criminal cases where it is plaintiff, appears in actions on the validity of laws and issuances, initiates action to enforce contracts, deputises government legal officers with their head of office's concurrence, and — on the Chief Minister's directive — represents the Bangsamoro in international litigation, negotiations and conferences. The Legal Research and Opinion Division advises the Chief Minister and Cabinet, reviews and drafts executive issuances and decisions reversing a ministry head, drafts and reviews contracts, and formulates and reviews policy on Shari'ah matters, providing written Shari'ah opinions to the Chief Minister and Cabinet. There are also Intergovernmental Relations and Administrative and Finance Divisions.

Sections 12–13 — All legal officers of the Office and of the ministries form the Legal Liaison Network, chaired ex officio by the Attorney-General. Ministries engaging a private practice lawyer must notify the Attorney-General for records purposes, and may request legal service in writing — which may be provided only where no conflict of interest arises and the agency lacks the legal capacity itself.

Sections 14–16 — The Attorney-General manages the Office's budget, which the Bangsamoro Government transfers and releases directly. Ministries may seek the Attorney-General's opinion on matters involving constitutional issues. All ministries must notify the Attorney-General of all litigation within 3 days, and no case may be filed or commenced on behalf of the Bangsamoro Government without prior notice.

Section 17 — No criminal, civil or administrative suit shall be brought against the Attorney-General, the Assistant Attorney-General or a subordinate officer in respect of any proceeding in a court of law or in the course of discharging the functions of the Attorney-General under the act; and where an official function is exercised in good faith, they shall not be personally liable for any action, claim or demand whatsoever.

Section 19 — An initial ₱15,000,000 for Personal Services and ₱3,000,000 for initial operation, sourced from the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund and the Contingent Fund, with subsequent funding in the Bangsamoro Appropriations Act.
Section 23 — Takes effect 15 days after complete publication in at least one newspaper of general circulation in the region.

related_legislation.related_note: Created pursuant to Section 8, Article XVI of the Organic Law (RA 11054). Its oath-administering power references Section 41(2), Chapter 10 of Executive Order 292, the national Administrative Code.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The page footers of the signed copy misnumber the act as BAA 7; the heading and the official index give it as BAA 5.

citizen_questions.a: Acts as the Bangsamoro Government's own lawyer — advising the Chief Minister, Cabinet and ministries, drafting and reviewing contracts and issuances, and representing the government in court. It is not a prosecutor.

Yes. Section 9 allows the Attorney-General to require any officer or employee to furnish information, and to summon any of them — except Members of Parliament and their immediate staff — to explain or assist, including case build-up.

citizen_questions.q: Does the Attorney-General handle Shari'ah questions?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. The Legal Research and Opinion Division formulates and reviews policy on Shari'ah matters to ensure compliance with Shari'ah rules and principles, and provides written Shari'ah opinions to the Chief Minister and the Cabinet.

citizen_questions.q: Is the Attorney-General independent of the Chief Minister?
citizen_questions.a: No. The Chief Minister appoints, and Section 5 makes the appointment coterminous with the appointing authority on the basis that the position is primarily confidential.

Section 17 bars criminal, civil or administrative suits against the Attorney-General, the Assistant and subordinate officers in respect of proceedings or the discharge of functions under the act, and shields them from personal liability where the function was exercised in good faith.
